before: A literal type describes one exact value. "open" | "closed" is a union: a value may match either alternative. The vertical bar belongs to the type description; it does not concatenate strings or execute a choice.
state = "ajar" is rejected because that exact string is not an alternative. This catches an unintended value before execution. It does not mean data arriving from a file has already been validated.
Define Pace as "steady" | "quick". Define pace with that type and set its value to "steady". Its type must allow either supported pace but reject other spellings.
after: A literal type means one exact value. A union joins allowed types with `|`, meaning or. So `"open" | "closed"` allows either of those two text values.
Assigning `"ajar"` causes a type error because it is not listed. If that becomes a real supported choice, add it to the type. Outside data still needs checks while the program runs.
Define Pace to allow exactly `"steady"` or `"quick"`. Give pace that type and start it at `"steady"`.
